summary: Move /admin off Clerk auth onto tailnet-membership trust
description:
## Motivation

Clerk production keys are domain-locked at the SDK level — they refuse to initialize when `window.location.host` doesn't match the registered production domain ("Clerk: Production Keys are only allowed for domain 'guru-ai.org'"). The tailnet hostname `guru-web-prod.tailb5626e.ts.net` is a separate DNS root, so Clerk hard-rejects there. Clerk's Multi-domain / satellite-domain feature would unlock additional hosts but is a paid plan upgrade.

The original BRD-admin-ui §1.2 cited Clerk middleware as the "third gate" in defense in depth (after Caddy public-listener rewrite and tailnet-only routing). That third gate was structurally impossible on the free Clerk plan once the app moved to live keys — discovered during the 2026-05-09 production cutover.

## Approach

Drop Clerk auth on `/admin` and `/api/admin` entirely. Trust comes from being on the tailnet. Caddy already routes the tailnet hostname to the app; that listener is the gate.

## File-by-file changes

- **src/middleware.ts** — remove the admin block (no more allowlist check, no more iat ceiling). Middleware reverts to no-op for /admin paths. The `clerkMiddleware` wrapper stays since other paths still use Clerk.
- **src/lib/admin.ts** — rename `requireAdmin()` → `requireTailnet()`. Returns either a synthetic operator object (id="tailnet", email="admin@tailnet") or 404. Trust signal: a Caddy-injected `X-Tailnet-Trust` header for belt-and-suspenders, since trusting deployment topology alone is fragile to future routing changes.
- **src/app/(admin)/layout.tsx** — drop the `{operator.email}` display (just say "ADMIN") or pull from a single `ADMIN_DISPLAY_EMAIL` env var if attribution is wanted back without Clerk.
- **src/__tests__/admin.test.ts** — rewrite. Drop iat-ceiling tests. New tests assert: tailnet trust signal yields the synthetic operator; absence yields 404.
- **deploy/Caddyfile** — tailnet listener block adds `header_up X-Tailnet-Trust 1`. Public listener also strips any inbound `X-Tailnet-Trust` header (defense against an attacker setting it from the public side). The existing public-listener `/admin → /admin-404` rewrite stays in place — that's the second gate.
- **Tailscale ACL** (out-of-repo, in Tailscale admin panel) — tag admin-capable devices explicitly (e.g. `tag:admin-device`) instead of "everyone on the tailnet." Document the tag in deploy/README.md so the tag → /admin-access mapping is recoverable across operator handoffs.

## Risks and mitigations

- **Defense-in-depth collapses to the Caddy listener split.** Mitigation: keep the public-listener `/admin → /admin-404` rewrite (already in deploy/Caddyfile lines 27-28). That's the second gate.
- **Identity attribution disappears.** Mitigation: `ADMIN_DISPLAY_EMAIL` env var if a name is wanted in the amber bar. Acceptable to skip until a second admin exists.
- **Tailnet membership is more persistent than a Clerk session.** Mitigation: configure Tailscale device expiry / require periodic re-auth at the Tailscale level. Out of repo but document in deploy/README.md.
- **Local dev needs a bypass** since dev devs aren't on the tailnet. Mitigation: `requireTailnet()` returns the synthetic operator unconditionally when `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'`. Pin with a test.
- **Future routing path that doesn't go through Caddy could forge X-Tailnet-Trust.** Mitigation: Caddy strips inbound `X-Tailnet-Trust` on the public listener before adding it on the tailnet listener.
- **Removes the iat ceiling that limits long-lived signed-in sessions.** Mitigation: this becomes Tailscale's job (device expiry / key rotation policy).

## Test plan

- Existing `src/__tests__/admin.test.ts` rewritten to cover the new model.
- Test asserting middleware no longer touches /admin paths (regression against accidentally leaving the old block in).
- Test asserting `requireTailnet()` returns 404 when `X-Tailnet-Trust` is absent and operator object when present.
- `NODE_ENV=development` bypass test.
- Manual smoke after deploy: hit /admin via tailnet (works) and via guru-ai.org (404, Caddy intercepted).

## Related

- Discovered during go-live cutover 2026-05-09 (PR #54).
- The forceRedirectUrl bug in PR #55 is in the public-domain sign-in flow and is independent of this refactor.
- Once this lands, `ADMIN_USER_IDS` env var becomes vestigial — remove from /etc/guru-web.env and from any docs.
